I'm a liberal professor, and my liberal students terrify me

Reaching my last week of college at UC Santa Cruz, I've seen my fair share of student-professor (sometimes TA) confrontations. One of the most recent was in a general ed. Greek mythology section. We were discussing gender portrayals and planning a a short skit at the end of class. As discussion eventually led way to joking, a few jokes were made regarding skirts and women (I can't quite remember). A classmate who identified as trans got upset and left the class. The TA was distraught and we elected to talk a little about what happened. The issue was clear in that feelings were upset when people began to turn the discussion into a mockery. I assume that if we held the discussion "civil" and polite we might have avoided the issue and the problem would be solved. Yet this issue really isn't solved, as Schlosser points out our education system is incredibly bureaucratic, administratively dense with multiple departments (non-educational) managing conduct and numbers over "education". Specifically its reflected in how the environment is such where professors are easily axed by a trigger happy administration as soon as red flags emerge. Schhlosser also doesn't mention the atmosphere in which some schools operate, typically undergrad/graduate schools where professors are kept on a short leash of deadlines and research submissions to keep their standing and/or job.

I feel for Schlosser, it must not be easy for him to have to deal with a barrage of conflicted emotions because heck, alot of these college kids are in an integral moment of realization and discovery. Some people cope with new knowledge better than others. Is it right for Scholsser to expound on the vices of a society where students are running a supposed fear campaign and professors should fear for their jobs and the ethics of free speech? When (of course this is just my opinion) personally I feel to shift the scope of scrutiny on the student needs to be juxtaposed onto the administration for handling the matter in which serious consequences are always delivered, rather than reach a more understanding position? I realize I'm generalizing a lot in this response so please forgive me if you can
